paymentPlan.label: Payment plan
paymentPlan.loanFormula: — computed from the {{loanType}} loan formula: {{rate}}% a.m. over {{term}} months{{sacNote}}.
paymentPlan.extraAmortization: {{cadence}} — extra amortization from the "{{name}}" recurring bill, on top of the installment above.
paymentPlan.automatic: — inferred from the average of your {{count}} linked repayments.
paymentPlan.noneFewPayments: No schedule yet — fewer than two repayments are linked, so there's no cadence to infer.
paymentPlan.noneTooVaried: No schedule — the linked repayments vary too much to infer a reliable amount.
paymentPlan.noneStaysOut: This debt stays out of cash-flow projections until a payment bill is linked below{{suffix}}.
paymentPlan.noBillsAvailable: No confirmed bills available to link yet.
paymentPlan.noBillsLinked: No bills linked yet — link one below to make this debt's payment explicit.
paymentPlan.overrideLabel: Don't infer a schedule from payment history (use only the bills above)
paymentPlan.overrideTitle: Skip the payment-history heuristic even if it would otherwise pass — useful once the bills above are already accounting for this debt's payments.
paymentPlan.footerLoan: A formal loan's monthly installment always comes from the loan formula, unchanged — but any bill linked here counts as an extra amortization payment on top of it, paying the balance down (and off) faster than the plain schedule alone.
paymentPlan.footerOther: Every linked bill's amount and cadence adds to this debt's expected payment, bounded by what's still remaining — explicit, instead of only inferred from history.
paymentPlan.noProjectedPayments: No projected payments in the next {{horizon}} months{{suffix}}.

trajectoryChart.titleWithRate: Growing with interest vs being paid off
trajectoryChart.avoided: of interest avoided so far — untouched, this debt would be {{ifUnpaid}} today instead of {{actual}}.
trajectoryChart.notEnoughHistory: Not enough history to chart yet — once a couple of repayments are linked, this debt's balance-over-time chart appears here.
trajectoryChart.canPayOffNote: You can pay off here: {{month}} — the earliest month your projected cash balance alone covers everything still owed on this debt, principal and interest, without waiting for the regular schedule to finish it off.
trajectoryChart.captionFuture: This debt hasn't started yet, so there's no real history — the whole line is projected{{source}}, starting from its own start date.
trajectoryChart.captionWithRate: The rust line is this debt compounding at {{rate}}% a month with nothing ever paid; the green line is the balance with payments — solid where real{{source}}. The gap between them is what paying it down is worth.
trajectoryChart.captionWithRateSourceSchedule: , dashed where projected from the loan's own schedule
trajectoryChart.captionWithRateSourceBill: , dashed where projected from the linked payment bill
trajectoryChart.captionWithRateSourceHeuristic: , dashed where projected from your recent average payment
trajectoryChart.captionPlain: The remaining balance as each repayment posted — solid where real{{source}}.
trajectoryChart.captionPlainSourceBill: , dashed where projected from the linked payment bill
trajectoryChart.captionPlainSourceHeuristic: , dashed where projected from your recent average payment
trajectoryChart.totalInterestLifetime: Total interest over the life of this debt
trajectoryChart.notTrueEndOfLoan: The planned payment doesn't clearly outpace interest, so this is only a running total through the charted horizon above, not a true end-of-loan figure.

overviewChart.title: All debts — balance over time
overviewChart.caption: Every debt summed by direction — rust is what you owe, green is owed to you (kept separate, not netted). Solid is real history; dashed carries each debt forward on its own schedule or recent payments, holding flat where there's nothing to project from.

balanceScheduleChart.title: What's still owed — principal vs. interest
balanceScheduleChart.caption: Both reach zero together right at payoff. Only exact for a formal loan (rate + PRICE/SAC schedule on file) — a debt paid down by a linked bill or inferred from history shows entirely as principal, since there's no formula to split it from.

page.futureNote: Hasn't started yet — its start date is still ahead.
page.addDebtDescription: A fixed principal is for a simple loan. A split percentage is for a shared expense you fronted (e.g. a house-build cost split 50/50) — link the shared purchase transaction(s) as "borrow"/"lend" and the amount owed grows automatically as you link more.
